status_summary: DHS revoked Harvard's SEVP certification on 2025-05-22 and Proclamation 10948 (signed 2025-06-04) suspended for six months entry of new Harvard F, M and J students, but a federal court blocked the revocation on 2025-06-20 and the proclamation on 2025-06-23, and DHS later stipulated it would not enforce the revocation. In late May 2025 the Secretary of State said the department would work with DHS to revoke visas of Chinese students with party ties or in critical fields and would add scrutiny to future applications from China and Hong Kong. DHS published a final rule on 2026-07-17, effective 2026-09-15 subject to congressional review, replacing duration of status for F and J holders with fixed admission periods of up to four years; the parts read show no nationality-based limit for students. Entry limits for nationals of listed countries under Proclamations 10949 and 10998 are covered in c06-05.

timeline.event: DHS revoked Harvard's SEVP certification; Harvard sued the next day.

The Secretary of State said the department would work with DHS to revoke visas of Chinese students with Chinese Communist Party ties or in critical fields, and would revise criteria to add scrutiny to future applications from China and Hong Kong.
Proclamation 10948 suspended for six months entry of foreign nationals coming to study at or join exchange programs at Harvard, and directed review of Harvard's SEVP participation.

A federal district court issued a longer-term injunction against the Harvard proclamation; the SEVP revocation had been blocked on 2025-06-20, and DHS stipulated on 2025-08-06 that it would not enforce it.
DHS proposed replacing duration of status for F, J and I nonimmigrants with fixed admission periods.
DHS published the final fixed-period-of-admission rule for F, J and I nonimmigrants, effective 2026-09-15 and classified as a major rule.

title: Put national security first in SEVP and cut student visas for adversary-country nationals
uncertainties: The Harvard litigation timeline comes from a science-policy organization's page last updated 2026-03-15, which lists the proclamation as expired and does not mention appeals. The NPR article does not state the announcement date; 2025-05-28 is taken from its URL. The final rule was read in large part: it caps F and J admission at program length up to four years and mentions an exception for some I nonimmigrants from the PRC, and no country-based limit for students was seen; whether it took effect on 2026-09-15 after congressional review was not confirmed. No source on the actual change in visa issuance to Chinese students was found. A DHS proposed rule of 2026-10-08 on Optional Practical Training fees is not national security related and is not counted.
